 Bed Rails, Infant Bouncers and Bike Helmets Among Nine Product Recalls
 Free Press Publisher 
 November 19, 2026 
 Notices 
 The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced nine recalls on Nov. 19, 2026, covering portable bed rails, infant bouncers, bicycle helmets, children’s pajamas, trade tools, magnetic toys, off-road vehicles, dry bags and rechargeable battery packs. Consumers should stop using the recalled products immediately and follow the instructions below.
 Xentrawave adult portable bed rails. About 2,114 rails were recalled because users can become trapped within the rail or between the rail and mattress. The CPSC received one report of an 89-year-old woman who died of asphyxiation after becoming trapped between a model XT016 rail and her mattress. For a full refund, cut the foam padding on the handle grips and submit a photo through the recall page or email it to xentrawavedirect@163.com .
 Kidsview infant bouncers. About 412 bouncers were recalled because they can collapse during use. Kidsview received seven reports of collapses, including two in which an infant’s head struck the surface below. One consumer sought medical attention for their infant. Affected date codes begin with 2022/08, 2022/09 or 2022/10 and appear on the back of the seat. For an Amazon gift card, mark the fabric seat “RECALLED” in permanent marker and email a photo showing the marking and date-code label to haimaoziying@163.com .
 Cipton bicycle helmets. The recall covers 16,730 white youth-size small helmets, model CPSK300CC. The helmets fail federal requirements for impact protection, stability and certification and may fail to protect riders in a crash. For a full refund, cut the straps, mark the helmet “Recalled” in permanent marker and email a photo to Reply@customersupport123.com . Consumers can also call 888-588-1629 or visit the recall page .
 Qpancy children’s pajama sets. About 1,309 sets were recalled because they fail federal children’s sleepwear standards and pose a serious burn hazard. For a full refund, cut the pajamas in half, email a photo to qpancyrecall@outlook.com and dispose of the cut pajamas.
 Hultafors Group North America trade tools. About 229,430 lighted portfolios, digital angle locators, digital calipers and building calculators were recalled. Children can easily access the button batteries, and the products and packaging lack required warnings. Swallowed button batteries can cause internal burns, serious injury or death. Keep the tools away from children and follow local hazardous waste procedures for the batteries. For a refund issued as a virtual Visa gift card, upload a photo and confirm disposal on the recall page . Contact Hultafors at 877-722-7026 or HultaforsGroup7307@sedgwick.com .
 CHE-US magnetic robot toys. About 101,282 sets of magnetic stick figures were recalled because high-powered magnets can come loose from the figures’ limbs. Swallowing the magnets can cause serious internal injuries or death. Keep the toys away from children. For a full refund, email a photo showing the toys in the trash to CHE-USMagneticRobotToysRecall@outlook.com .
 Vanderhall Brawley GTS electric off-road vehicles. Vanderhall recalled 220 vehicles because the brakes can engage while the vehicle is airborne and lock when it lands. Owners should contact their dealer or Vanderhall for instructions on installing firmware version 8.1.2 through the company’s mobile app. Vanderhall can also be reached at inquiry@vanderhallusa.com .
 Fidlock Hermetic dry bags. About 490 bags were recalled because the closure strips can detach and release magnets that can cause serious injury or death if swallowed. Submit a photo through the recall page , then dispose of the bag. Fidlock offers a replacement or an online store gift card. Customers who bought directly from Fidlock’s online store can receive a full refund. Contact Fidlock at 888-303-8332 or recall_2608@fidlock.com .
 Ororo rechargeable lithium-ion battery packs. About 269 packs were recalled in the United States and another 24 in Canada because they can overheat, posing fire and burn hazards. Register on the recall page for a full refund and disposal instructions. Contact Ororo at 702-751-7639 or recall@ororowear.com .
 The CPSC says to keep the recalled Cipton helmets and Ororo battery packs out of household trash, curbside recycling and retail battery collection boxes. Call your local household hazardous waste facility before bringing either product to confirm that it accepts defective or recalled lithium-ion batteries.

 The Franklin County Free Press, established by Vicky Taylor in 2019, emerged as a beacon of local journalism for the residents of Franklin County. Under Vicky's leadership, it quickly became an essential source of news, particularly at a time when major newspaper publications were increasingly overlooking local coverage. 
On January 1, 2022, the torch was passed to Nathan Neil and his firm, Neil Publishing, LLC. Neil, a local entrepreneur with multiple thriving businesses in Chambersburg, shares Vicky's fervent commitment to both the community and the world of local journalism. 
Rooted in the heart of Franklin County and powered by its residents, the Franklin County Free Press continues to bridge the gap, ensuring that the local stories, events, and issues that matter most to the community remain in the spotlight.
